title: RECEIVER TECHNIQUES AND ALGORITHMS FOR PNT SOLUTIONS WITH ONLY 1 AND 2 LEO SATELLITES IN VIEW - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view, based on the optimised fusion ofall the available estimations along time.Description: The use of LEO-based systems on top of current GNSS systems (in MEO orbits) is being considered to improve the achievable user performances, in particular in challenging user scenarios. To ensure that at least3 or 4 satellites are in view by any user on ground, a much larger number of LEO satellites than for MEO is required to be used inthis case. In this context, it is of high interest to investigate techniques exploiting signals received by LEO satellites when only 1 and 2 LEO satellites are in view by a ground user. This would enable, for example, to exploit LEO satellites with reduced constellations with a limited available number of satellites visible, and/or while a full LEO-PNT constellation is still being deployed. Theobjective of this activity is to design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view,, including transitions between 1 and 2 satellites, based on the optimised fusion of all the available estimations along time, including at least:- ToA (Time-of-Arrival), FoA (Frequency-of-Arrival) and AoA (Angle-of-Arrival)-like estimations; - Multi-epoch / synthetic apertureprocessing solutions exploiting the fast satellite geometry change; and, additionally, if introducing benefits to the above : - Clock coasting; - Inertial sensors measurements; - DEM (Digital Elevation Model)/height sensors ; The suitability of the proposed solutions is aimed to be assessed based both on simulations and real data. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define and design innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Develop the required tools/software for the assessment/test of the innovative techniques and algorithms; - Assess/test the different techniques and algorithms in realistic simulated conditions, and with real signals from LEO satellites; - Identify the most promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained;- Propose the way-forward to further mature each of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. title: N2O SATELLITE OBSERVATION REQUIREMENTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. This study aims at characterising the needs for space-based observations of atmospheric N2O, starting from a user and science perspective. Knowledge gaps are identified related to the N2O production and life cycle, its impact on stratospheric ozone, and its role in the Earth's radiation balance that can be addressed with the help of satellite observations, with a focus on information that can be provided from satellite observations. The study explores the space of requirements that satellite observations of atmospheric N2O (Level-2) and measurements of radiances at the top of the atmosphere (Level-1) would have to meet in order to contribute to addressing these knowledge gaps.

title: GT1D-613SY - METHODOLOGY TO UPDATE OPERATIONAL MODELS OF A SPACECRAFT SYSTEM (EXPRO+)
description: Simulation models developed at design, AIT and operations phases shall be recalibrated based on the flight experience. Currently, during operation, the predictive simulations performed by design, AIT and operations teams with simulators are not fully connected toflight telemetry. Therefore, the simulators do not reflect the real state of the spacecraft and the lessons learned are not transferred to the models for the next spacecraft. The activity aims at streamlining the process, enhancing the fidelity and representativeness of the simulation models and reducing the effort for models update and reusability. In this activity, to implement the correction of the model, an assessment to define the origin of the deviation shall be made considering the latest advancement in digitalization, model calibration and synchronization, leveraging the concepts of digital twins' spacecraft. Furthermore, state of the art approaches of surrogate modelling, AI and Machine Learning shall be considered to enhance representativeness and fidelity. The experimentation plan shall be extended in a multidisciplinary way, to improve the method, including in-flight data, and to prepare multidisciplinary optimization to improve operations, future design and reduce the margins.

title: LOW COST AND HIGH EFFICIENCY DEPLOYABLE RADIATOR FLAP FOR TELECOM CONSTELLATION SATELLITES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a low cost and high efficiency deployable radiator flap based on 2-phase technology (based on evaporation-condensation of a fluid to transport heat) for satellites constellations.Description: A small telecom platform operating in LEO (Low Earth Orbit) will require additional surface area to radiate heat, hence necessitating the deployment of radiator flap(s). These radiator flaps will need to be low cost and will utilize two-phase equipment to efficiently transport heat from the main radiator to theflaps. This activity will assess the use of flexible heat pipes or low-cost loop heat pipes. Several technologies will be evaluatedand the one that offers the best flexibility and scalability for high aspect ratio satellites will be selected. The assembly of the2-phase equipment with the flap will also have to be studied, as well as the flap technology itself (material, coating) to meet mass, performance and integration requirements (stowed and deployed configuration). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation. - Technologies trade off review and baseline selection. - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard demonstrator. - Validation testing of the breadboard demonstrator.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: PHOTONICS-BASED OPTICAL APERTURE FOR LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.056) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a thin optical aperture leveraging advances in integrated photonic technology to reduce the size andweight of space-based optical communication terminals.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of both size and weight of satellite laser communication terminals by 50%.Description: Optical communication terminal solutions with lower size and weight are required to serve the increasing role of small spacecraft for satellitecommercialisation by maximising the amountof payload space for mission-enabling processing or sensors. State-of-the-art optical communicationterminals are often too bulky and heavy for such small platforms and a leap in technology is required. This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
